## Participation

The Participation plugin records class participation. Ask Claude to open it and you get your class as a grid: a score of 1 to 3 for how much each student spoke, another for quality, and a note if you want one. Saving writes a row per student to `participation.csv` in that class's folder.

All it needs is a list of names. Photos are optional --- where you have them students appear as faces, and where you don't, as initials.

Key features:

- Set up from what you already have. Claude reads your class list --- a spreadsheet, a CSV, a text file, a list you paste into chat --- and builds the roster from it. If you also have a photo roster or a folder of headshots, it uses those for the pictures. Nothing has to be converted into a particular format first.
- A row per student per class meeting. Anyone left unscored is recorded as a 0, so a saved class is complete rather than a set of blanks to interpret later. Re-saving a date replaces that class's rows, so correcting a score is the same operation as entering it.
- Your records stay in your folder. `participation.csv` sits in the class folder with the rest of the course material, in a format Excel opens directly. For term totals or a gradebook column, ask Claude --- it reads the file and does the arithmetic.
- Runs locally. Inside Academic Studio the app opens in an in-editor tab; elsewhere, a browser tab. No account, no upload, and no model calls from the app itself, so student names and photos stay on your machine.

### Requirements

- A list of your students' names, in whatever form you have it.
- Python (installed via Help → Run Setup… in Academic Studio).

### Installation

Open Help → Run Setup…, follow the "Teaching & research plugins" link, and check Participation. One click installs it, and Python is on the same screen under Supporting programs. The first time you use it, Claude asks where you keep your class folders and what your class lists look like, then remembers both.

Run Setup is also where updates appear --- it flags a new version of the plugin when one is available, so you don't need to download a new copy of Academic Studio to get it. The installed plugin lives in your shared Claude configuration, so it works from Claude Code CLI and the Code mode of Claude Desktop too.

Academic Studio is not required. The plugin is published in the [kerryback/skills](https://github.com/kerryback/skills) marketplace, so you can install it into Claude Code directly:

```
/plugin marketplace add kerryback/skills
/plugin install participation@kerryback-skills
```

Adding the marketplace is a one-time step --- every other plugin on this site installs from it the same way. The same two commands work from a terminal without an interactive session, as `claude plugin marketplace add kerryback/skills` and `claude plugin install participation@kerryback-skills`.
